extracted.intended_audience: employers, immigration attorneys, HR professionals, and USCIS adjudicators handling H-classification petitions (H-1B, H-2A, H-2B, H-3, H-1C)
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards governing validity, denial, revocation, extensions, admission limits, exemptions, and procedural requirements for H-classification (H-1B, H-2A, H-2B, H-3, H-1C) petitions filed with USCIS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labor condition application corresponding to requested validity period
rubrics_metrics.description: If the petition requests new dates of employment after the labor condition application already submitted with the H-1B petition, the petitioner must submit a certified labor condition application with a new validity period that properly corresponds to the new requested validity period on the petition and an updated prevailing or proffered wage, if applicable, except that the petitioner may not reduce the proffered wage from that originally indicated in their petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This labor condition application may be certified after the date the H-1B petition was filed with USCIS. The request for new dates of employment and submission of a labor condition application corresponding with the new dates of employment, absent other changes, will not be considered a material change. An increase to the proffered wage will not be considered a material change, as long as there are no other material changes to the position.

rubrics_metrics.name: RFE on requested dates — effect on approval and benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: If USCIS does not issue an RFE concerning the requested dates of employment, if the petitioner does not respond, or the RFE response does not support new dates of employment, the petition will be approved, if otherwise approvable, for the originally requested period or until the end-date eligibility has been established, as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, the petition will not be forwarded to the Department of State nor will any accompanying request for a change of status, an extension of stay, or amendment of stay, be granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-1B specialty-occupation validity period
rubrics_metrics.description: An approved petition for an alien in a specialty occupation shall be valid for a period of up to three years but may not exceed the validity period of the labor condition application.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-1B DOD research/coproduction validity period
rubrics_metrics.description: An approved petition for an alien involved in a DOD research and development project or a coproduction project shall be valid for a period of up to five years.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-1B fashion modeling validity period
rubrics_metrics.description: An approved petition for an alien of distinguished merit and ability in the field of fashion modeling shall be valid for a period of up to three years.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-2B petition validity equals approved temporary labor certification
rubrics_metrics.description: The approval of the petition to accord an alien H-2B classification shall be valid for the period of the approved temporary labor certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-3 trainee validity period
rubrics_metrics.description: An approved petition for an alien trainee classified under H-3 shall be valid for a period of up to two years.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-3 special education participant validity period
rubrics_metrics.description: An approved petition for an alien classified as a participant in a special education training program shall be valid for a period of up to 18 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-1C registered nurse validity period
rubrics_metrics.description: An approved petition for an alien classified under H-1C shall be valid for a period of 3 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-1B petitions for beneficiary-owned entities limited duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial approval of a petition filed by a U.S. employer in which the H-1B beneficiary possesses a controlling interest (owns more than 50% or majority voting rights) will be limited to up to 18 months. The first extension (including an amended petition requesting extension of stay) of such a petition will also be limited to up to 18 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-4 dependent admission and employment-authorization eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Spouse and children accompanying/following-to-join an H nonimmigrant may be admitted as H-4 nonimmigrants for the same period as the principal. H-4 status does not confer employment authorization incident to status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An H-4 spouse may be eligible for EAD only if the H-1B is beneficiary of an approved Immigrant Petition for Alien Worker (or successor) or the H-1B's period of stay authorized under sections 106(a) and (b) of AC21. To request employment authorization, an eligible H-4 spouse must file Form I-765 (or successor) with documentary evidence establishing eligibility, including spousal relationship and proof of the principal's qualifying status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial for multiple beneficiaries
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for multiple beneficiaries may be denied in whole or in part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial for inaccurate, fraudulent, or materially misrepresented statements
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition will be denied if statements on the petition, the H-1B registration, the application for temporary labor certification, or the labor condition application were inaccurate, fraudulent, or misrepresented a material fact, including if certifications on the registration are false.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An H-1B cap-subject petition also will be denied if it is not based on a valid registration submitted by the petitioner (or designated representative) or a successor in interest for the beneficiary named or identified in the petition. A valid registration must represent a bona fide job offer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial for attempt to unfairly increase chance of selection
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS may deny a subsequent new or amended petition filed on behalf of the same beneficiary if it determines the filing is part of an attempt to unfairly increase the chance of selection during registration or petition selection process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: changing the proffered wage in a subsequent petition to an amount equivalent to a lower wage level than that indicated on the registration or original cap-subject petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of denial and appeal rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner will be notified of the reasons for denial and of the right to appeal the denial under 8 CFR part 103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no appeal from a decision to deny an extension of stay to the alien.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory denial for certain H-2A/H-2B violators
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS will deny any H-2A or H-2B petition filed by a petitioner (or successor) that has been the subject of specified actions such as a final administrative debarment by the Secretary of Labor, or a final USCIS denial/revocation with a finding of fraud or willful misrepresentation issued during pendency or within 3 years prior to filing (with temporal applicability for petitions filed on/after Jan 17, 2025).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies if the debarment or final determination occurs on or after Jan 17, 2025 and the petition is filed on or after that date and during the debarment period, or if revocation/denial decision was on a petition filed on/after Jan 17, 2025.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretionary denial for H-2A/H-2B where compliance questioned
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS may deny an H-2A or H-2B petition (filed on/after Jan 17, 2025) if it determines the petitioner (or successor) has not established intention and/or ability to comply with H-2A/H-2B program requirements, considering prior actions or violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violation examples include revocation of temporary labor certification, debarment, other administrative sanctions, revocation by USCIS for untrue statements or failure to employ beneficiary as specified, or findings of violation of employment-related laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors considered in assessing petitioner’s intent/ability to comply
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS will consider all relevant factors including: recency and number of violations; egregiousness (number of workers affected, health/safety risk); pattern/history of violations; severity/monetary penalties; findings of willfulness; extent of financial gain or worker injury; timely compliance with penalties/remedies; and corrective actions taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution of convictions/determinations to petitioner
rubrics_metrics.description: A criminal conviction or final administrative/judicial determination against certain individuals will be treated as against the petitioner or successor in interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes an individual acting on behalf of the petitioning entity (owner, employee, contractor) or, for paragraph (h)(10)(iv)(B), an employee whom a reasonable H-2A or H-2B worker would believe is acting on behalf of the entity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of prior adjudication finding petitioner can comply
rubrics_metrics.description: If USCIS previously determined in an adjudication that a petitioner (or preceding entity) established intention and ability to comply notwithstanding relevant violations, USCIS will not deny a subsequent petition based on the same prior violation determination(s) unless it learns a new material fact or finds a material error of law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitioner notification and obligation to report changes (revocation context)
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner shall immediately notify the Service of any changes in terms and conditions of employment of a beneficiary which may affect eligibility under section 101(a)(15)(H) and paragraph (h) of this section. An amended petition should be filed when the petitioner continues to employ the beneficiary; if no longer employed, petitioner shall send a letter explaining the change(s) to the director who approved the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: H-2A and H-2B petitioners have specified notification duties to DHS under their respective paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director’s authority to revoke petitions at any time
rubrics_metrics.description: The director may revoke a petition at any time, even after the expiration of the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate and automatic revocation triggers
rubrics_metrics.description: Approval of any petition is immediately and automatically revoked if the petitioner goes out of business, files a written withdrawal of the petition, or the Department of Labor revokes the labor certification upon which the petition is based. The approval of an H-1B petition is also immediately and automatically revoked upon notification from the H-1B petitioner that the beneficiary is no longer employed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for revocation on notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The director shall send a notice of intent to revoke if he or she finds that: beneficiary no longer employed in capacity specified; statement(s) of facts in petition/registration/temp labor certification/LCA were not true/correct or were fraudulent; petitioner violated terms and conditions of approved petition; petitioner violated requirements of section 101(a)(15)(H) or paragraph (h); approval violated paragraph (h) or involved gross error; H-1B cap-subject petition not based on valid registration; petitioner failed to timely file amended petition notifying USCIS of a material change; or the petitioner filed new/amended petition to unfairly increase chance of selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of intent to revoke — process and rebuttal
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice shall contain a detailed statement of grounds for revocation and the time period allowed for petitioner's rebuttal. The petitioner may submit evidence in rebuttal within 30 days of receipt of the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The director shall consider all relevant evidence presented in deciding whether to revoke in whole or in part. If revoked in part, remainder remains approved and a revised approval notice will be sent with the revocation notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of H-2A/H-2B petition revocation on beneficiary's status
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon revocation of approval of an employer's H-2A or H-2B petition, the beneficiary and their dependents will not be considered to have failed to maintain nonimmigrant status, and will not accrue unlawful presence under section 212(a)(9) solely on the basis of the petition revocation for a 60-day period following revocation, or until the end-date of authorized admission, whichever is shorter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During such period, the alien may only work as otherwise authorized under 8 CFR 274a.12. The employer will be liable for reasonable costs of return transportation to the beneficiary's last place of foreign residence, unless the alien obtains an extension of stay based on an approved petition in the same classification filed by a different employer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal rights for denials and revocations
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition denied in whole or in part may be appealed under part 103. A petition revoked on notice in whole or in part may be appealed under part 103. Automatic revocations may not be appealed.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-3 admission period and pre/post admission days
rubrics_metrics.description: An H-3 beneficiary will be admitted for the validity period of the petition, plus up to 10 days before the validity period begins and 10 days after the validity period ends. The beneficiary may not work except during the validity period of the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to reside outside U.S. after maximum period of stay
rubrics_metrics.description: When an alien in H classification has spent the maximum allowable period of stay in the U.S., a new petition may not be approved unless that alien has resided and been physically present outside the U.S., except for brief trips, for the time limit imposed on the particular H classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brief trips for business or pleasure are not interruptive but do not count toward required time abroad. For H-2A and H-2B certain periods of absence provide a new total of 3 years; the petitioner must provide information about employment, place of residence, and dates/purposes of trips during required residence abroad.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-2A/H-2B cessation-of-employment protection period
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien admitted or provided H-2A/H-2B status and their dependents will not be considered to have failed to maintain nonimmigrant status, and will not accrue unlawful presence, solely on the basis of a cessation of the employment on which classification was based, for 60 consecutive days or until the end of authorized admission, whichever is shorter, once during each authorized period of admission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During such period, the alien may only work as otherwise authorized under 8 CFR 274a.12.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to apply for extension or change of status if otherwise eligible
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien in any authorized period may apply for and be granted an extension of stay under 8 CFR 214.1(c)(4) or change of status under 8 CFR 248.1, if otherwise eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-1C maximum admission period rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The maximum period of admission for an H-1C nonimmigrant is 3 years; periods of time spent outside the U.S. during validity count toward the maximum; upon reaching 3-year maximum, the H-1C alien is no longer eligible for admission as H-1C.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-1B six-year (and DOD project 10-year) limitation and recapture rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An H-1B alien in a specialty occupation (or fashion modeling) who has spent six years in the U.S. under sections 101(a)(15)(H) and/or (L) may not seek extension/change/ readmission unless the alien has resided and been physically present outside the U.S. for the immediate prior year. An H-1B alien involved in DOD research/coproduction who has spent 10 years may not seek extension/change/readmission for such services unless resided and been physically present outside the U.S. for the immediate prior year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time spent physically outside the U.S. exceeding 24 hours during validity of an approved H-1B petition shall not be considered for purposes of calculating total period of authorized admission and may be recaptured in a subsequent petition. It is petitioner's burden to request and demonstrate recapture with evidence (passport stamps, I-94, airline tickets, chart referencing independent documentary evidence). USCIS may grant all, part, or none of recapture requested. If beneficiary was previously counted toward the numerical cap with respect to the 6-year maximum, a petition seeking recapture will not subject beneficiary to the cap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lengthy adjudication delay exemption to 6-year limit
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien in or who previously held H-1B status is eligible for status beyond 6 years if at least 365 days have elapsed since filing of a labor certification (if required) or the filing of an immigrant visa petition on the alien's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approvals under this exemption may be granted in up to 1-year increments until a final decision is made to deny/revoke the labor certification or immigrant visa petition, deny/approve the alien's application for immigrant visa or adjustment, or administratively close the application. A decision is not final while appeal is available or pending. Petition may be filed within 6 months of the requested H-1B start date; petitioner need not be the employer that filed the labor certification/immigrant petition. Substitution of beneficiaries before July 16, 2007 has limits. Aggregation of days from multiple filings to meet 365-day requirement is not permitted. Only the principal beneficiary of a nonfrivolous labor certification/immigrant petition may be eligible. Limits apply on future exemptions if beneficiary fails to file adjustment within 1 year of visa authorization (USCIS may excuse for circumstances beyond control).

rubrics_metrics.name: Per-country limitation exemption to 6-year limit
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien who maintains or previously held H-1B status and is beneficiary of an approved immigrant visa petition under section 203(b)(1),(2),(3) and who is eligible for that immigrant status but for per-country limitation is eligible for H-1B beyond 6 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioner must demonstrate visa unavailability as of filing date. USCIS may grant validity periods in increments up to 3 years while alien remains eligible. Approvals may be granted until final decision to revoke the immigrant visa petition or until immigrant visa/adjustment decision. Current H-1B status not required; subsequent petitioners may seek exemptions; may file within 6 months of requested start date; only principal beneficiary eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-3 limitation on admission and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: An H-3 special education program participant who has spent 18 months in the U.S. and an H-3 trainee who has spent 24 months in the U.S. may not seek extension/change/readmission unless resided and been physically present outside the U.S. for the immediate prior 6 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions exist for H-1B and H-3 aliens who did not reside continually in the U.S. and whose employment was seasonal or intermittent or aggregate of 6 months or less per year, and for commuters who reside abroad and regularly commute to the U.S. To qualify for exception, petitioner and alien must provide clear and convincing proof (e.g., arrival/departure records, tax returns, records of employment abroad).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of visa petition validity — Form I-129 requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner must file a request for a petition extension on Form I-129 to extend the validity of the original petition under section 101(a)(15)(H) of the Act. A request for petition extension generally may be filed only if the validity of the original petition has not expired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of stay — general rules and filing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner shall apply for extension of an alien's stay by filing a petition extension on the form prescribed by USCIS accompanied by the documents described for the particular classification. The petitioner must also request a petition extension. The dates of extension shall be the same for the petition and the beneficiary's extension of stay. The beneficiary must be physically present in the U.S. at time of filing. Director shall make separate determinations on petition and extension of stay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the alien is required to leave the U.S. while extension requests are pending, petitioner may request the director to cable notification of approval to the consular office abroad where alien will apply for a visa. When the total period of stay in an H classification has been reached, no further extensions may be granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of stay — H-1C specific
rubrics_metrics.description: H-1C alien maximum period of admission is 3 years. An H-1C initially admitted for less than 3 years may receive an extension up to the third anniversary date of initial admission. An H-1C may not receive extension beyond the third anniversary date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of stay — H-1B specific
rubrics_metrics.description: An extension of stay may be authorized for up to three years for an H-1B beneficiary in a specialty occupation or fashion modeling; the alien's total period of stay may not exceed six years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request for extension must be accompanied by either a new or a photocopy of the prior certification from the Department of Labor that the petitioner continues to have on file a labor condition application valid for the period requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of stay — H-1B DOD project
rubrics_metrics.description: An extension may be authorized for up to five years for an H-1B beneficiary involved in a DOD research and development or coproduction project; the total period of stay may not exceed 10 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of stay — H-2A/H-2B specific
rubrics_metrics.description: An extension of stay for H-2A or H-2B beneficiaries may be authorized for the validity of the labor certification or for a period up to one year, except as otherwise provided. The alien's total period of stay as an H-2A or H-2B worker may not exceed three years (except in the Virgin Islands where total may not exceed 45 days).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of stay — H-3 specific
rubrics_metrics.description: An extension of stay may be authorized for the length of the training program for a total period as an H-3 trainee not to exceed two years, or as a participant in a special education training program not to exceed 18 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of permanent labor certification approval or filing of immigrant petition on H classification
rubrics_metrics.description: The approval of a permanent labor certification or the filing of a preference petition for an alien shall not be a basis for denying an H-1C or H-1B petition or a request to extend such a petition, or the alien's admission, change of status, or extension of stay.
